links.outcome: Model performance under surveillance perturbations and distribution-shift stress tests
links.effect: Delayed or less frequent reporting tolerated in some settings; threshold calibration fragile under more severe observation changes; partial-observation performance less stable across shifts.
links.quote: Surveillance stress tests further showed that delayed or less frequent reporting can be tolerated in some settings, but threshold calibration becomes fragile under more severe observation changes.

links.outcome: Performance when trained in shifted regime versus zero-shot transfer
links.effect: Training directly in the shifted regime improved performance compared with zero-shot transfer; portability across regimes can still improve, especially under partial surveillance data.
links.quote: When models were trained directly in the shifted regime, performance improved compared with zero-shot transfer, indicating that the digital twin can adapt to new and previously unseen operating conditions but that portability across regimes can improve, particularly when only partial surveillance data are available.

screen.reason: The study develops and stress-tests a hospital AMR digital twin (graph neural network/transformer combined with mechanistic simulation) under surveillance perturbations, missing observations, and distribution shifts to evaluate robustness and calibration before deployment.

primary.practice: distribution-shift stress testing and surveillance perturbations
